newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-WEST INDIES SKITTLE INDIA FOR ASTONISHING WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES SKITTLE INDIA FOR ASTONISHING WIN.

text.p: West Indies staged a remarkable third test victory over India on Monday.
Set just 120 to win and two days to achieve it, India were dismissed for a paltry 81.
The pace trio of Franklyn Rose, Curtly Ambrose and Ian Bishop tore through the fragile Indian batting as only opener Venkata Laxman reached double figures with 19.
Bishop completed the unexpected victory when he yorked Venkatesh Prasad to finish with four for 22 off 11.5 overs. It was India's lowest total in a Caribbean test.
Rose, who started the rout with three wickets in the first hour of the day, ended with three for 19 in nine overs. Ambrose weighed in with three for 36.

It was the 16th consecutive time a victory has been achieved at Kensington Oval and gave the West Indies a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. The first two tests in Jamaica and Trinidad were drawn. The fourth test stats in Antigua on Friday.

The win brought back memories of the West Indies' famous 52-run victory in their first test against South Africa in 1992 when the Springboks were bowled out for 148 after starting the final day on 122 for two, just 79 short of victory.
It also marked the first test victory as captain for Brian Lara, leading the West Indies for the first time after replacing the injured Courtney Walsh.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul, who hit his maiden century, 137 not out in the West Indies first innings total of 298, was named man-of-the-match.
Resuming on two without loss, India immediately lost opener Navjot Singh, caught at slip off Rose.
Rose, playing in only his third test, then had Rahul Sravid caught behind for two after occupying the crease for 36 minutes.
Rose then claimed his 15th wicket of the series, bowling the defiant Laxman, who had survived 77 minutes.
Skipper Sachin Tendulkar followed, brilliantly caught by Lara for four, then Ambrose returned for a third spell to bowl Saurav Ganguly and Mohammad Azharuddin with deliveries which kept low.
India's batsmen failed to show the necessary discipline and when Anil Kumble scooped a simple catch to Roland Holder at square leg they were 57 for seven.
After all-too-brief resistance, the tail was wrapped up after lunch to secure a famous victory.
